Header.AppealFrom: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division

Counsel.Lead: Martin Porter KC; Anastasia Karseras (instructed by Bolt Burdon Kemp)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant contends that the learned Deputy High Court Judge erred in finding that the Respondent highway authority had established the statutory defence afforded by section 58 of the Highways Act 1980. The Judge further erred in dismissing the common law negligence claim regarding the absence of signage indicating the end of the shared cycle path.

FactsReliedOn.item: On 22 April 2020, the Appellant was riding his mountain bike on a path adjacent to the A10 carriageway near Cheshunt, separated by a grass verge.
The Appellant encountered a jogger travelling in the same direction and moved onto the grass verge to overtake safely.
There was a concealed hole in the grass verge which caused the Appellant to be thrown from his bicycle.
The Appellant sustained serious injuries including a complex fracture of the second cervical vertebra, requiring him to give up his employment as a social worker.
The Respondent's highway inspector, Mr Cooke, claimed to have conducted a walked inspection on 13 February 2020 but GPS data from his vehicle showed he only stopped once for three minutes.
Mr Cooke did not attend trial, having retired, and the Respondent served a Civil Evidence Act Notice less than three weeks before trial.

Contentions.item: The learned judge erred in finding that the Respondent had established the statutory defence under section 58 of the Highways Act 1980.
The GPS evidence demonstrated that Mr Cooke could not have performed a walked inspection of the relevant area on 13 February 2020.
The judge erred in treating Mr Cooke's witness statement evidence as credible when it was manifestly inconsistent with contemporaneous GPS data.
The Respondent owed a common law duty of care to erect signage indicating the end of the shared cycle facility.
It was foreseeable that cyclists would use the grass verge to pass other highway users.

LegalBasis.item: Highways Act 1980, Section 41 (duty to maintain highways)

ReliefSought.item: An order allowing the appeal against the lower court's decision dismissing the claim.
A finding that the Respondent failed to establish the section 58 defence.
A declaration that the Respondent breached its duty under section 41 of the Highways Act 1980.
Damages for the injuries sustained by the Appellant.

A cyclist using the grass verge to pass another highway user was plainly foreseeable and represented ordinary use of the highway.
